title: Computer and Information Systems Managers
description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities in such fields as electronic data processing, information systems, systems analysis, and computer programming.

tasks.text: Manage backup, security and user help systems.
Develop computer information resources, providing for data security and control, strategic computing, and disaster recovery.
Develop and interpret organizational goals, policies, and procedures.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Assign and review the work of systems analysts, programmers, and other computer-related workers.
Evaluate data processing proposals to assess project feasibility and requirements.
Review project plans to plan and coordinate project activity.
Direct daily operations of department, analyzing workflow, establishing priorities, developing standards and setting deadlines.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Meet with department heads, managers, supervisors, vendors, and others, to solicit cooperation and resolve problems.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Provide users with technical support for computer problems.
Recruit, hire, train and supervise staff, or participate in staffing decisions.
Stay abreast of advances in technology.
Consult with users, management, vendors, and technicians to assess computing needs and system requirements.
Evaluate the organization's technology use and needs and recommend improvements, such as hardware and software upgrades.
Review and approve all systems charts and programs prior to their implementation.
Prepare and review operational reports or project progress reports.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Apache Maven, C, Canu, Common business oriented language COBOL.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, Blackboard software, FileMaker Pro, Langlais Computer Consultants CalMan.

skills.name: Enterprise application integration software
skills.def: Software to connect different business systems to improve scalability or streamline work flows. Examples: Enterprise application integration EAI software, Extensible markup language XML, IBM InfoSphere DataStage, Oracle Fusion Middleware.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Adobe Flex, Apache Tomcat, Backbone.js, Drupal.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Advanced business application programming ABAP, Borland Paradox, C#, C++.

skills.name: Data base management system software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or provide access to a set of related information. Examples: Alpha Four, Apache Cassandra, Apache Hadoop, Apache Pig.
